correctness.rationale: The unit-oscillator half-kick/drift/half-kick map is M(h)=[[1−h²/2,h],[−h(1−h²/4),1−h²/2]], det 1; direct multiplication verifies M(h)^T diag(1−h²/4,1) M(h)=diag(1−h²/4,1), positive for 0<h<2, so constant-step powers are bounded. For any distinct support timesteps a,b, independent symbolic computation verifies trace(M(a)M(b)M(a)^−1M(b)^−1)=2+a²b²(a−b)²(a+b)²/16>2, making the generated subgroup noncompact. No finite invariant set of real lines exists: singleton would give a real eigenline of elliptic A/B; a two-line set would force both matrices traceless and a=b=sqrt(2); ≥3 lines would force finite projective action inconsistent with a hyperbolic commutator. Bounded M(h) and inverse on (0,2) ensure integrable log norm; the classical Furstenberg theorem then gives an almost-sure strictly positive top norm Lyapunov exponent for every iid non-point law, and the strong law converts this to physical-time growth λ/EH>0. The point-mass exponent is zero. Independent exact check gives trace(M(1)M(6/5))=−347/250 within (−2,2), so that deterministic alternation is bounded. Finite exact checks confirm identities, not the probabilistic theorem.
